This is meaningful only if the feedback settles rather than grows without bound. Earlier work tested that loop by loop, requiring each feedback loop, or loops meeting at a common variable, to stay below a critical strength; such tests are only approximate, and where loops share no variable they can accept an unstable system or reject a stable one. This paper instead gives a spectral and pseudospectral treatment of the rock engineering interaction matrix, drawing on recent developments in non-normal matrix analysis and robust-stability theory from numerical linear algebra. The global interaction matrix is the resolvent (I - A)⁻¹ of the interaction matrix A, and the coupled system is stable exactly when the spectral radius ρ(A), the largest eigenvalue magnitude, is below one. Two margins measure how far a stable system sits from instability: a multiplicative margin independent of the variables&apos; units, and a pseudospectral margin that reveals the non-normality the eigenvalues conceal. Closed-form expressions rank the mechanisms that most move the stability boundary. The framework is demonstrated on Jiao and Hudson&apos;s six-variable dam foundation and nine-variable hydroelectric pressure tunnel, reproducing their published global matrices, and it extends to larger multi-domain systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7194881\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1142/s0218339095000381\", \"title\": [\"FEEDBACK LOOPS, STABILITY AND MULTISTATIONARITY IN DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p> By fairly simple considerations of stability and…

The framework is demonstrated on Jiao and Hudson&apos;s six-variable dam foundation and nine-variable hydroelectric pressure tunnel, reproducing their published global matrices, and it extends to larger multi-domain systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7194881\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1142/s0218339095000381\", \"title\": [\"FEEDBACK LOOPS, STABILITY AND MULTISTATIONARITY IN DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p> By fairly simple considerations of stability and multistationarity in nonlinear systems of first order differential equations it is shown that under quite mild restrictions a negative feedback loop is a necessary condition for stability, and that a positive feedback loop is a necessary condition for multistationarity. </jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1142/s0218339095000381\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1995, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/s0143385710000878\", \"title\": [\"Structural stability of attractor–repellor endomorphisms with singularities\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We prove a theorem on the structural stability of smooth attractor–repellor endomorphisms of compact manifolds, with singularities. By attractor–repellor, we mean that the non-wandering set of the dynamics <jats:italic>f</jats:italic> is the disjoint union of an expanding compact subset with a hyperbolic attractor on which <jats:italic>f</jats:italic> acts bijectively.
